title: Social inequalities in family time and money use for child-rearing in Hungary
title_hu: Társadalmi egyenlőtlenségek a gyermeknevelési célú családi idő- és pénzfelhasználásban Magyarországon
summary_en: Do richer Hungarian families spend more on their children — both in money and in parental time? Hajdú, Kertesi and Kézdi use Hungarian time-use and household-budget surveys to document the income gradient in childcare-time and child-rearing expenditures. They find a strong gradient in monetary spending but a smaller and reversed gradient in some categories of parental time, and discuss the implications for child-development outcomes and for the design of family-support transfers.
policy_relevance: Direct relevance for Hungarian family-policy design (EMMI, Belügyminisztérium családpolitika): the paper informs the choice between cash-transfer vs. in-kind-service family policies — cash transfers narrow the monetary gradient but may not reach the time-use channel. Useful input for the calibration of the családi adókedvezmény, GYED, and bölcsőde-availability policies.
